vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: polymarket-simmer-fastloop
Version: 1.0.8

The skill is a functional automated trading bot for Polymarket fast markets. The Python script (polymarket-simmer-fastloop.py) implements a mean reversion strategy using price data from Binance and institutional flow data from NOFX (nofxos.ai). It includes legitimate features such as daily budget tracking, local market caching to handle API latency, and volatility-adjusted position sizing. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection was found; all network and file operations are consistent with the stated purpose of a trading tool.

llm.summary: The skill is a plausible Polymarket trading bot whose code and runtime instructions align with the advertised purpose, but there are packaging/metadata inconsistencies and a few operational details (writing caches, requiring private-key env for live trading) that warrant extra caution before installing or running live.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and the provided Python file implement a Polymarket/Simmer trading strategy (momentum + order-book filters) and use the Simmer SDK and Polymarket CLOB endpoints as expected. Required capabilities (SIMMER_API_KEY, TRADING_VENUE, optional WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY for live) are coherent with a trading skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions remain within the trading scope: obtaining a Simmer API key, running the script in paper or live mode, scheduling via cron, and caching market IDs/ledger/daily spend to disk. The skill writes several files (fast_markets_cache.json, fastloop_ledger.json, daily_spend.json) into its folder — expected for a trading agent but worth noting. SKILL.md asks users to set WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY for live trading (normal) and warns not to share it.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with a Python source file and a declared pip dependency (simmer-sdk). The dependency is a normal public pip package; there are no downloads from obscure hosts or archives in the manifest.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill legitimately requires SIMMER_API_KEY and TRADING_VENUE and may use WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY for live execution. However, the top-level registry metadata (presented to you) claims "Required env vars: none" and "Primary credential: none", which contradicts SKILL.md and clawhub.json (which list SIMMER_API_KEY and TRADING_VENUE). This metadata mismatch is a packaging/integrity concern because a user could be misled about which secrets are needed. Also, providing a WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY in environment variables to any third-party code carries real risk — confirm how the Simmer SDK signs transactions locally before giving keys to this skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and is user-invocable. It writes its own ledger/cache files to its directory and suggests scheduling via cron/OpenClaw. These are reasonable for a trading bot, but remember that if you enable cron or run --live the skill can execute trades autonomously — ensure you understand and trust the code before granting live credentials.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to be a real Polymarket/Simmer trading bot and its code generally matches the README, but: 1) do not trust the registry-level metadata that claimed no env vars — the skill needs a SIMMER_API_KEY and TRADING_VENUE and may require your WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY for live trading; 2) review the full Python source yourself (or have someone audit it) before supplying any private key or enabling live/cron runs; 3) prefer running in paper mode (--live not used) until you have validated behaviour and logs (use --stats and --resolve); 4) if you must test live, use a wallet with minimal funds or a delegated signing arrangement (hardware wallet or limited-account key) and verify that the Simmer SDK performs local signing and does not send your raw private key to external endpoints; 5) verify the simmer-sdk package source/version you will install; 6) check the skill folder for the cache/ledger files (they will be written locally) and consider running in an isolated session/container to limit blast radius.
